current.name: Prof. Carl Soulsbury
current.role: Professor of Animal Ecology · Group leader
current.text:
My main interest is the evolution of life history strategies. My work focuses mainly on the behavioural and evolutionary ecology of vertebrates, but has expanded to include plant and insect life histories.

I did my undergraduate degree at the University of Aberdeen, where I was awarded the Nicol Prize for the top zoology graduate. I then did a PhD on red fox *Vulpes vulpes* dispersal at the University of Bristol, supervised by Prof. Stephen Harris and Dr Phil Baker, followed by a postdoc on black grouse behavioural ecology at the University of Jyväskylä. I am now Professor of Animal Ecology at the University of Lincoln.

current.name: Karen Salazar Niño
current.text: Karen holds a Marie Curie Fellowship studying collective sperm movement.

current.name: Georgia Freer
current.text: Georgia is doing her PhD with Blake Morton, Simon Clegg and me on the welfare of urban animals, focusing on parasites and pathogens.

current.name: Sophie Ackhurst
current.text: Sophie's project looks at the biomechanics of ageing sperm and how this may relate to cryptic female choice.

current.name: Jess Frith
current.text: Jess works on our HFSP-funded project on the evolution of sperm morphology in insects. She previously did a BSc in Bioveterinary Science at the University of Lincoln.

current.name: Himara Van Haevermaet
current.text: Himara's PhD with Prof. Daniel Mills looks at dog aggression and the signals used by aggressive dogs.

current.name: Beverley Wilson
current.text: Bev's PhD with Prof. Daniel Mills is on fear and frustration in dogs.

former.name: Rebecca Chen
former.role: PhD, viva May 2026 · Hoffman lab, Bielefeld
former.text: Rebecca's PhD used state-of-the-art sequencing to unravel the genetic architecture of sexually selected traits in the lekking black grouse *Lyrurus tetrix*, including inbreeding depression and the role of DNA methylation. Co-supervised with Joe Hoffman and Kees van Oers.

former.name: Dr Ruben Culqui Salazar
former.text: Ruben's PhD looked at caecilian distribution and ecology in Ecuador.

former.name: Dr Hafiza Maira Munir
former.text: Maira's PhD was on lesser wax moths.

former.name: Libbi Gray
former.text: Libbi studied floral phenotypes and how they may be affected by changes in UV-B radiation, using herbarium specimens and greenhouse and growth-chamber experiments. She went on to a PhD at the University of Edinburgh.

former.name: Jess Dobson
former.text: Jess studied the quality of sexual signals in male black grouse: carotenoid pigments in the red eye combs (HPLC and microtomy), and how feather structure influences colour. She is now doing a PhD with Prof. Matthew Shawkey at Ghent University.

former.name: Dr Matti Kervinen
former.text: Matti studied the ecological factors affecting lifetime fitness of black grouse males, separating what contributes most to variation in reproductive success and survival at different ages. He now works for the Finnish Wildlife Agency (Riistakeskus).

former.name: Dr Ben Chivers
former.text: Ben completed a PhD with Prof. Fernando Montealegre-Z, using µ-scanning laser Doppler vibrometry in a large comparative study of stridulation and wing mechanics across katydid species.

former.name: Sarah Harris
former.text: Sarah studied the red eye combs of black grouse and how they relate to female mate choice, heritability and individual scheduling of growth. She went on to work as a research assistant on the PEARL project.

former.name: Christian Pulver
former.text: Christian measured the mechanical contribution of the multiple acoustic ports to a single katydid ear, using three laser systems and several species with different ear morphology.

former.name: Dan Veitch
former.text: Dan worked with Fernando Montealegre-Z on how sound velocity is reduced in the acoustic trachea of bush-crickets, using *Copiphora gorgonensis* as a model.

former.name: Ed Woodrow
former.text: Ed studied changes in deer damage in the Bardney Limewoods, combining historical records and surveys.

former.name: Ellie Smith
former.text: Ellie studied harvest mouse ecology and distribution, assessing the state of populations and extrapolating across the UK.

former.name: Eini Nieminen
former.text: Eini studied temporal scheduling of male lekking effort in black grouse, finding that young males increased effort as older males spent less time on the lek. She went on to a PhD at the University of Jyväskylä.

former.name: Anssi Lipponen
former.text: Anssi joined the black grouse project as a trainee in 2005, did his BSc on magpie microsatellites, worked as a laboratory technician, and completed an MSc developing a nested qPCR method for blood parasite loads in black grouse. He went on to a PhD at the University of Eastern Finland.
